notes: Fictional staff handbook. Facts are invented so the chat model cannot answer from pretraining. Each question names the single passage that contains the answer.

documents.title: Annual leave
paragraphs: The company year for holidays runs from 1 March to 28 February. Unused plans should be discussed in the February team meeting.
Full-time staff receive 18 days of annual leave, plus public holidays. Part-time staff receive a pro-rata share of those 18 days.
At most 5 days may be carried into the next company year, and carried days must be used before 31 May.
Leave requests need 10 business days of notice. The manager confirms or declines in writing within 3 business days.
Leave already approved can be cancelled by the company only when a client deadline was agreed in the statement of work.

documents.title: Sick leave
paragraphs: Sick leave is separate from annual leave and does not reduce the 18-day holiday balance.
Full-time staff may take 10 days of paid sick leave in a company year. Unused sick days expire on 28 February and are not paid out.
A medical note is required after 2 consecutive sick days, and it should be sent to the manager before the third day.
Same-day sick notice goes to the manager by 09:30 local time. A colleague covering a client call should be named in that message.
Elective appointments should be booked outside core hours where the clinic allows it.

documents.title: Parental leave
paragraphs: Parental leave applies to birth, adoption, and long-term foster placement.
The primary caregiver may take 16 weeks of paid parental leave. The secondary caregiver may take 4 weeks.
Notice of 8 weeks is required before the planned start date, sent to both the manager and payroll.
During paid parental leave the company continues pension contributions at the same rate as the prior month.
A return-to-work conversation is booked in the week before the caregiver comes back.

documents.title: Everyday expenses
paragraphs: Everyday expenses cover meals and supplies bought while working a normal office day, not client trips.
A meal on a working day is reimbursed up to 42 dollars. Anything above that is paid by the employee.
A receipt is required for any everyday expense over 25 dollars. Smaller amounts need a card statement line.
Expense reports are due within 14 days of the purchase. Payroll rejects reports filed after that.
Office supplies over 100 dollars need a written note from the office manager before purchase.

documents.title: Client travel
paragraphs: Client travel means a trip booked to visit a client site outside the home city.
Client entertainment is reimbursed up to 75 dollars per person, and the client names must be listed.
Alcohol on a client meal is reimbursed up to 20 dollars per person. Amounts above that are personal.
Travel bookings need written approval from the engagement lead before the ticket is bought.
Hotel nights are capped at 180 dollars before tax. Breakfast included in the rate does not count as a separate meal.

documents.title: Account security
paragraphs: Work accounts are issued by IT on the first morning. Personal email is not a login for client systems.
Passwords must be at least 14 characters and are changed every 180 days.
Multi-factor authentication is required on email, the VPN, and the client file store.
Laptops must use full-disk encryption, BitLocker on Windows and LUKS on Linux, before the first client file is copied.
A lost laptop is reported to IT within 1 hour. IT revokes sessions the same day.

documents.title: Client file retention
paragraphs: Client files include contracts, invoices, and working papers stored in the project folder.
Client contracts and invoices are kept for 7 years after the engagement ends.
A client's written deletion request is completed within 30 days, except where the 7-year rule still applies.
Staff must not send client files to a personal email address or a personal cloud drive.
Working drafts that were never sent to the client may be deleted when the engagement closes.

documents.title: On-call rotation
paragraphs: The on-call rotation covers production incidents for hosted client work.
The weekly on-call stipend is 180 dollars, paid with the next salary run.
The person on call answers a page within 15 minutes, at any hour during the assigned week.
The rotation starts each Monday at 09:00 local time and ends the following Monday at 09:00.
Swap requests are sent to the engineering lead at least 48 hours before the week begins.
